inputs.original_text: Five months after a ceasefire was announced in Gaza, airstrikes are still killing civilians, and the humanitarian situation remains dire There is little left that connects Palestinians in Gaza with their prewar existence. The contours of life have become darker and far more brutal, as if the population has been stripped from its past. “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen,” said 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five currently displaced in Deir al-Balah. Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: The ceasefire was announced five months ago, but civilians are still being killed by airstrikes, and people in Gaza remain exposed to drones, gunfire, shelling, and fire directed at fishermen. That gap between the official label and lived reality isn’t an accident—it lets powerful institutions present a story of progress while the destruction continues out of sight. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says the drones “never stop buzzing overhead.” The ceasefire sounds less like peace than a convenient narrative for making ongoing violence easier to overlook.
